{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVlzVyc8AAAABiyrY-g", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BqjeczhMJTWY", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bqjec", "number": 28, "title": "Simplify the core tool set around command execution and patch-based editing", "body": "## Goal

Simplify Cognix's model-facing tool set using Codex's approach: reuse existing OS commands for general operations and provide a dedicated tool for controlled file edits. Avoid implementing a separate Rust tool for every operation already supported by existing utilities.

## Current behavior

`src/schema.rs` exposes five tools: `list_files`, `read_file`, `apply_patch`, `create_file`, and `run_command`. The patch tool requires the SHA-256 from a previous `read_file` call. Runtime command approval is now supported following #26, but the command tool is still described as a verification-only tool.

## Expected outcome

Reduce the core model-facing tool set to two responsibilities:

- General command execution (`run_command` or `exec_command`): use existing commands such as `ls`, `cat`, `rg`, and test runners for project exploration, reading, searching, and verification. Make invocation practical without requiring the model to know machine-specific absolute executable paths; resolve executables safely. Prefer reusing the existing command runtime. Full shell syntax, pipelines, and interactive process sessions are not required for this change.
- File editing (`apply_patch`): provide one simple patch interface for file creation and modification, and support deletion/moves where safely implemented. Keep explicit preview and approval for edits; detect stale changes internally rather than making the model obtain a SHA-256 through a dedicated read tool. Use Codex's patch interface as a reference, not a requirement to reproduce all of its implementation.

Remove redundant model-facing `list_files`, `read_file`, and `create_file` once their use cases are covered. Internal helpers may remain where useful.

Preserve the project boundary, runtime approvals, optional command allowlist, cancellation, timeouts, output limits, and sandbox isolation established by #26 and earlier work. Keep command execution read-only with respect to the project; file mutations should go through the patch tool. No unsandboxed fallback or silent expansion of permissions. If an existing safety restriction prevents a desired command, handle it explicitly rather than bypassing it.

Keep the design small; do not introduce a new framework, a generalized tool abstraction, or a complex patch protocol merely to achieve parity with Codex. The existing internal patch-v2 implementation is not a requirement for the new interface.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The model receives a small tool set centered on general command execution and patch-based editing; redundant tools are no longer advertised.
- [ ] From an ordinary project directory, Cognix can list files, inspect source, and search text using existing utilities, with the applicable runtime approval and sandbox policy.
- [ ] Cognix can create and edit files through the unified patch tool, with a clear preview, approval, and protection against overwriting unrelated or stale changes. Document any unsupported patch operations explicitly.
- [ ] The existing zero-division example succeeds using only the new core tools and reports actual test evidence. Exercise file creation too.
- [ ] Focused tests cover denied commands/patches, path boundaries, stale edits, and execution failures. Update the system prompt, tool definitions, and README to match the new behavior.

## Reference

- [Codex core tool registration](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs)
- [Codex apply_patch implementation](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/apply-patch)

No implementation changes have been made in this issue.
